claims.text: Adding approximately 10 at.% Al to an elemental Cr coating on Zircaloy-4 will improve coating durability under both normal subcritical-water and high-temperature steam conditions.
Approximately 10 at.% Al promotes formation of a continuous, dense oxide scale.
The Al-modified oxide scale retards oxygen diffusion.
The Al modification limits Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Elemental Cr coatings on Zircaloy-4 undergo Cr-Zr interdiffusion and premature failure in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The oxide scale produced by a coating containing approximately 10 at.% Al contains Cr2O3 and Al2O3.
The oxide scale may contain TiO2 if Ti is present.
Al preferentially oxidizes to form a stable, adherent Al2O3 layer at approximately 10 at.% Al.
Approximately 10 at.% Al does not disrupt beneficial Cr2O3 formation.
Suppressing oxygen ingress and Cr-Zr interdiffusion maintains coating structural integrity and adhesion.
Al contents of at least 17 at.% lead to deleterious intermetallic phases.
Al contents of at least 17 at.% produce oxide discontinuities.
Al contents below the proposed optimum fail to stabilize the oxide scale sufficiently.
Relative to pure Cr, the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will have a lower oxidation rate in high-temperature steam.
Relative to pure Cr, the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will exhibit less oxygen penetration.
Relative to pure Cr, the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will exhibit less Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Reduced oxidation, oxygen penetration, and Cr-Zr interdiffusion will enhance coating integrity and adhesion.
A pure Cr coating develops premature failure at 1000 °C for 60 minutes because of extensive Cr-Zr interdiffusion and poor oxide-scale stability.
The proposed behavior is applicable to steam oxidation at 1000 °C for 60 minutes and, with more limited confidence, at 1100 °C for 30 minutes.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism claim protection under both normal subcritical-water and accident-relevant steam conditions, but the stated conditions and boundary include only high-temperature steam tests at 1000 and 1100 °C. No normal subcritical-water condition is specified or tested.
